questions.question:
In the `lunar` namespace scenario, you are tasked with creating a multi-stage Dockerfile.

A stub Dockerfile has been provided at `/tmp/exam/course/1/Dockerfile` and a simple `main.go` program at `/tmp/exam/course/1/main.go`.

Update the Dockerfile to have two stages:

1. The first stage should use `golang:1.20-alpine` as the base image. Name it `builder`.
   - Copy `main.go` into `/app/`.
   - Build it with `go build -o /app/server /app/main.go`.
2. The second stage should use `alpine:3.18`.
   - Copy the `server` binary from the `builder` stage to `/opt/server`.
   - Set the entrypoint to `/opt/server`.

You do not need to build the image, just ensure the `Dockerfile` is correctly defined.

verification.description: Builder stage defined (FROM golang:1.20-alpine AS builder)

questions.question:
Create a Pod named `data-processor` in the `crescent` namespace.

The Pod should run a main container using the `nginx:alpine` image named `main-app`.

The main container should only start AFTER an init container successfully completes its task. Add an init container named `wait-for-service` using the `busybox:1.36` image. The init container should run the command: `sh -c 'sleep 5 && echo "Dependencies ready"'`.

verification.description: Pod data-processor exists in crescent namespace

questions.question:
In the `twilight` namespace, create a CronJob named `nightly-backup`.

- Schedule: every 10 minutes (`*/10 * * * *`).
- Container image: `busybox:1.36`.
- Command: `sh -c 'sleep 30'`.
- Configure the CronJob to `Forbid` concurrent executions.

verification.description: CronJob nightly-backup exists in twilight namespace

questions.question:
A developer wants to use the Ambassador pattern for a legacy application. Create a Pod named `legacy-app` in the `eclipse` namespace.

1. Main container: Name it `backend`, use image `nginx:1.25`, and expose port 80.
2. Ambassador container: Name it `proxy`, use image `haproxy:2.8-alpine`.

(Note: we are just simulating the pattern, no advanced haproxy config is needed, just defining the two containers is sufficient).

verification.description: Pod legacy-app exists in eclipse namespace

Roll back the `api-release` release to its previous revision (revision 1).

questions.question:
Create a Deployment named `slow-start-app` in the `shadow` namespace.

- Replicas: 3
- Image: `nginx:1.24`
- To ensure no downtime during updates for this application that takes time to initialize, set `minReadySeconds` to `20`.

verification.description: Deployment slow-start-app exists in shadow namespace

questions.question:
A Deployment named `critical-processor` exists in the `nightfall` namespace. You have been instructed to pause the rollout of this deployment to investigate an issue.

Pause the rollout of the `critical-processor` deployment.

In `/tmp/exam/course/8/`, there is a base deployment file `deployment.yaml` and a `kustomization.yaml`.

Create a JSON patch file named `patch.json` in the same directory. The patch should add an environment variable `MODE=production` to the container named `web` in the Deployment `frontend`.

Then, update the `kustomization.yaml` to include this JSON patch targeting the Deployment `frontend`. You do not need to apply the Kustomization, just set up the files.

verification.description: Files kustomization.yaml and patch.json both exist

questions.question:
A Pod named `metrics-gatherer` in the `starlight` namespace is failing to start. Identify the issue and fix it. The pod should be running smoothly.

(Hint: The image name might be misspelled).

verification.description: Image corrected (no longer a non-existent image)

questions.question:
Find the Pod in the `kube-system` namespace that is consuming the most CPU. Write the name of the Pod into the file `/tmp/exam/course/10/cpu-usage.txt`.

(If multiple pods are similar, just record the top one based on `kubectl top`).

Note: `kubectl top` needs metrics-server. If it is unavailable, determine a reasonable top-CPU pod name and record it; scoring only checks that the file exists and is non-empty.

Create a Pod named `logger` in the `lunar` namespace.

The Pod should run a single container using the `busybox:1.36` image. It should run a script that outputs logs to `/var/log/app.log`: `sh -c 'while true; do echo "App is running" >> /var/log/app.log; sleep 5; done'`.

Configure a sidecar container in the same pod named `log-tailer` using `busybox:1.36` that reads from `/var/log/app.log` and outputs to stdout: `sh -c 'tail -f /var/log/app.log'`.

Use an `emptyDir` volume to share the `/var/log` directory between the two containers.

verification.description: Pod logger exists in lunar namespace

questions.question:
In the `crescent` namespace, a Secret named `db-creds` and a ConfigMap named `app-config` exist.

Create a Pod named `combined-app` using the `nginx:alpine` image. Use a single `projected` volume mounted at `/opt/config` to expose:

1. The `db-creds` Secret.
2. The `app-config` ConfigMap.

verification.description: Pod combined-app exists in crescent namespace

`version=v2.1.0`

Configure the ConfigMap to be immutable to prevent accidental changes.

questions.question:
Create a Pod named `secure-pod` in the `eclipse` namespace using the `nginx:alpine` image. Apply the following security constraints:

1. The pod must run as user ID `1000`.
2. The container must NOT allow privilege escalation (`allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`).
3. The container must have a read-only root filesystem.

(You may need to mount an emptyDir to `/var/cache/nginx` and `/var/run` to make nginx work with read-only rootfs).

verification.description: Pod secure-pod exists in eclipse namespace

A Pod named `token-reader` in the same namespace mounts this secret. No changes are required to the Pod, just update the Secret.

verification.description: Secret legacy-token token value is super-secret-v2
